rationale: A wins because it keeps four usable press shapes tied tightly to the supplied facts, especially “Glossier adds three fragrances as it pushes into 800 more Sephora doors,” which correctly turns a thin product fact into a trade angle with proof gates. B has bite, but “The beauty blog that became a brand is now a shelf-space negotiation” drifts into grand DTC-cohort feature land without supplied evidence. The difference is discipline: A asks for missing proof; B sometimes writes as if it already has it.
gaps_in_A: “in one step” slightly overstates the rollout; the update says expansion, not whether all 800 new doors go live at once.
“Story type: customer-story” for the Sephora at Kohl’s angle is mislabeled; it is a retailer/protagonist-shift angle, not a customer story.
The Kohl’s angle admits it “only stands apart if the Kohl’s door count is real and material,” which means it needs the split before it deserves equal billing.
gaps_in_B: “The beauty blog that became a brand is now a shelf-space negotiation” is padded abstraction; it recycles the DTC-to-wholesale story at feature altitude instead of adding a clean new protagonist.

“one of the few brands with a clean twelve-year arc from blog to national wholesale” is invented comparative context. The update gives a 2014 blog origin, not category rarity or a national-wholesale thesis.
“suburban strip-mall retail rather than mall-and-city Sephora” imports geography and shopper assumptions not in the update. Cute line, bad habit.

Refusing “Glossier expands its fragrance line with three new launches” throws away a viable beauty-trade angle; the supplied fact says first fragrance line extension, which is thin but real if tied to distribution.
